title: Michigan required provisions and property-casualty laws
summary: Michigan fire policy rules, appraisal, termination notices, the Essential Insurance Act, TRIA, producer terminations and the guaranty association.
objectives: Recall the minimums and deadlines every Michigan fire policy must include
Walk through Michigan appraisal and home insurance termination notice rules
Apply Essential Insurance Act eligibility, underwriting and declination rules
Know the key numbers for TRIA and the Michigan guaranty association

scenes.title: Michigan required provisions and P&C laws
scenes.subtitle: Fire policy rules, appraisal, notice periods, the Essential Insurance Act, TRIA and the guaranty association

beats.text: Michigan laws and required provisions are part of the exam's Basics section. In this lesson, we'll pin down their key numbers.
beats.say: Michigan laws and required provisions are part of the exam's Basics section. In this lesson, we'll pin down their key numbers.

scenes.title: Every Michigan fire policy must include
items: Actual cash value; fire and lightning
12:01 a.m. standard time, at the property
Pro rata or $25, whichever is greater
30 days after proof of amount of loss
1 year, or a longer policy period; tolled

beats.text: Michigan's fire policy law sets minimums: at least actual cash value at the time of loss, for direct loss by fire and lightning.
beats.say: Michigan's fire policy law sets minimums: at least actual cash value at the time of loss, for direct loss by fire and lightning.

beats.text: It takes effect at twelve-oh-one a.m., standard time, at the property's location.
beats.say: It takes effect at twelve oh one A M, standard time, at the property's location.

beats.text: The insured may cancel anytime; the insurer needs 10 days' notice, but home insurance has its own rules. Minimum earned premium: pro rata or $25, whichever is greater.
beats.say: The insured may cancel anytime; the insurer needs ten days' notice, but home insurance has its own rules. Minimum earned premium: pro rata or twenty-five dollars, whichever is greater.

beats.text: Loss is payable within 30 days after proof of the amount of loss, unless the fire-loss withholding law applies.
beats.say: Loss is payable within thirty days after proof of the amount of loss, unless the fire-loss withholding law applies.

beats.text: Suit must start within 1 year after the loss, or the policy's longer period, paused from notice of loss until formal denial.
beats.say: Suit must start within one year after the loss, or the policy's longer period, paused from notice of loss until formal denial.

scenes.q: Which of these is NOT a provision Michigan law requires in every fire policy?
choices: Coverage of at least actual cash value at the time of loss
Coverage suspended after 30 days of vacancy
Coverage taking effect at 12:01 a.m. standard time
Loss payable within 30 days after proof of the amount of loss
scenes.why: The statute requires the policy to state whatever conditions suspend or restrict coverage, but it does not mandate a 30-day vacancy suspension. The other three are required provisions.

beats.text: Which of these is NOT required in every Michigan fire policy? Pick an answer.
beats.say: Which of these is NOT required in every Michigan fire policy? Pick an answer.

reveal.text: The 30-day vacancy suspension. The law only requires the policy to state whatever conditions suspend or restrict coverage.
reveal.say: The thirty-day vacancy suspension. The law only requires the policy to state whatever conditions suspend or restrict coverage.

items.label: Written demand
items.detail: Either side, when they disagree on actual cash value or the amount of loss

items.label: Name appraisers: 20 days
items.detail: Each side picks a competent, independent appraiser within 20 days after the demand

items.label: Agree on an umpire: 15 days
items.detail: Otherwise a circuit court judge in the county of the loss or property picks one

items.label: Any 2 of 3 decide
items.detail: A written agreement by any two of the three sets the amount of loss

items.label: Costs
items.detail: Each side pays its own appraiser; the umpire and other costs are split equally

beats.text: Appraisal: when the insured and insurer disagree on actual cash value or the amount of loss, either can demand it in writing.
beats.say: Appraisal: when the insured and insurer disagree on actual cash value or the amount of loss, either can demand it in writing.

beats.text: Within 20 days, each side names an independent appraiser.
beats.say: Within twenty days, each side names an independent appraiser.

beats.text: If the appraisers can't agree on an umpire within 15 days, a circuit court judge in the county where the loss occurred or the property is located picks one.
beats.say: If the appraisers can't agree on an umpire within fifteen days, a circuit court judge in the county where the loss occurred or the property is located picks one.

beats.text: Any 2 of the 3 set the loss in writing. Each side pays its own appraiser; the umpire and other costs are split equally.
beats.say: Any two of the three set the loss in writing. Each side pays its own appraiser; the umpire and other costs are split equally.

scenes.title: A new homeowners policy, a quick exit
scenes.story: Jordan's new homeowners policy in Flint was issued 40 days ago. The insurer decides to end it for a reason other than nonpayment and mails notice today. Under the Essential Insurance Act, how soon can the termination take effect?

items.label: A termination?
items.detail: Yes: a refusal to continue to insure for a reason other than nonpayment

items.label: Usual notice for home or auto
items.detail: At least 30 days, stating the effective date and each specific reason

items.label: Mailed within the first 55 days?
items.detail: Yes, at day 40, so it can take effect 20 days after mailing

items.label: Compare
items.detail: Nonpayment: as the policy says. General casualty minimum: 10 days. Malpractice nonrenewal: 60 days.

scenes.answer: Under the Act, no sooner than 20 days after the notice is mailed.

beats.text: Jordan's new homeowners policy in Flint is 40 days old. The insurer mails notice to end it, not for nonpayment. Under the Essential Insurance Act, how soon can it take effect?
beats.say: Jordan's new homeowners policy in Flint is forty days old. The insurer mails notice to end it, not for nonpayment. Under the Essential Insurance Act, how soon can it take effect?

beats.text: That's a termination. It normally needs at least 30 days' written notice, not the fire policy's 10, giving each specific reason.
beats.say: That's a termination. It normally needs at least thirty days' written notice, not the fire policy's ten, giving each specific reason.

beats.text: But a notice mailed in the first 55 days after issue can take effect 20 days after mailing.
beats.say: But a notice mailed in the first fifty-five days after issue can take effect twenty days after mailing.

beats.text: So: no sooner than 20 days after mailing.
beats.say: So: no sooner than twenty days after mailing.

beats.text: Compare: nonpayment terminations follow the policy. The general casualty minimum is 10 days, and a malpractice nonrenewal needs 60.
beats.say: Compare: nonpayment terminations follow the policy. The general casualty minimum is ten days, and a malpractice nonrenewal needs sixty.

scenes.title: Essential Insurance Act: home insurance rules

items.label: Eligible person
items.detail: Owner-occupant or tenant; an owner-occupant of up to 4 units qualifies

items.label: Not eligible, for example
items.detail: Arson conviction within 5 years; property taxes delinquent 2 or more years

items.label: Condition, not age
items.detail: Underwriting may use physical condition, without regard to the age of the structure

items.label: No redlining
items.detail: No refusing or limiting coverage because of the location of the risk

items.label: Declinations
items.detail: Give each specific reason; oral applicants may request it in writing within 90 days

beats.text: Under the Essential Insurance Act, owner-occupants and tenants are eligible persons for home insurance, including an owner living in a building of up to 4 units, but not a landlord living elsewhere.
beats.say: Under the Essential Insurance Act, owner-occupants and tenants are eligible persons for home insurance, including an owner living in a building of up to four units, but not a landlord living elsewhere.

beats.text: Excluded, for example: an arson conviction within 5 years, or property taxes delinquent 2 or more years.
beats.say: Excluded, for example: an arson conviction within five years, or property taxes delinquent two or more years.

beats.text: Underwriting may use physical condition, but not the age of the structure, and never the location of the risk: that's prohibited redlining.
beats.say: Underwriting may use physical condition, but not the age of the structure, and never the location of the risk: that's prohibited redlining.

beats.text: Declined applicants get each specific reason; after an oral application, a written explanation if requested within 90 days.
beats.say: Declined applicants get each specific reason; after an oral application, a written explanation if requested within ninety days.

scenes.q: Under the Essential Insurance Act, which applicant is an eligible person for home insurance?
choices: Ana, who owns and lives in a 3-unit building in Lansing
Ben, who owns a rental house in Saginaw but lives elsewhere
Cal, who was convicted of arson 2 years ago
Dee, whose property taxes are 3 years delinquent
scenes.why: An owner-occupant of a dwelling of up to 4 units is eligible. A landlord who lives elsewhere is not; an arson conviction within 5 years or taxes delinquent 2 or more years exclude a person.

beats.text: Quick check. Which applicant is an eligible person for home insurance? Pick an answer.
beats.say: Quick check. Which applicant is an eligible person for home insurance? Pick an answer.

reveal.text: Ana: she owns and lives in a building of up to 4 units. Ben doesn't live there, and Cal's arson and Dee's taxes disqualify them.
reveal.say: Ana: she owns and lives in a building of up to four units. Ben doesn't live there, and Cal's arson and Dee's taxes disqualify them.

scenes.title: TRIA: the federal terrorism program
scenes.src: TRIA §§102(1),(7), 103(e), 108(a); 15 U.S.C. 6701 note (current law as of Oct 2026)

items.label: Losses must exceed this to certify an act
Federal share above the insurer deductible
Industry losses needed before federal payment

beats.text: TRIA created the federal Terrorism Risk Insurance Program. The Treasury Secretary certifies acts of terrorism, consulting the Homeland Security Secretary and the Attorney General.
beats.say: T R I A created the federal Terrorism Risk Insurance Program. The Treasury Secretary certifies acts of terrorism, consulting the Homeland Security Secretary and the Attorney General.

beats.text: Certification needs losses over $5 million.
beats.say: Certification needs losses over five million dollars.

beats.text: Each insurer's deductible is 20% of its prior-year direct earned premium. Above it, the federal share is 80%.
beats.say: Each insurer's deductible is twenty percent of its prior-year direct earned premium. Above it, the federal share is eighty percent.

beats.text: Federal payments need industry losses over $200 million, and the annual cap is $100 billion.
beats.say: Federal payments need industry losses over two hundred million dollars, and the annual cap is one hundred billion dollars.

beats.text: Under current law it ends December 31, 2027. Extension bills were pending in 2026, so recheck before your exam.
beats.say: Under current law it ends December thirty-first, twenty twenty-seven. Extension bills were pending in twenty twenty-six, so recheck before your exam.

scenes.title: When an insurer terminates a producer

items.label: Agreement silent?
items.detail: May service existing policies; may not bind, renew or increase the insurer's obligation without approval

items.label: Policyholders protected
items.detail: No cancel or nonrenew because the producer's contract ended

items.label: Home and auto: allowed reasons
items.detail: Malfeasance, breach of trust, Code violations, failure to perform, under 25 apps in 12 months

items.label: Not mainly for location
items.detail: Not based primarily on the producer's geographic location or loss experience tied to it

beats.text: If the agency agreement is silent, a terminated independent producer may keep servicing existing policies, but can't bind new risks, renew, or increase the insurer's obligation without approval.
beats.say: If the agency agreement is silent, a terminated independent producer may keep servicing existing policies, but can't bind new risks, renew, or increase the insurer's obligation without approval.

beats.text: The insurer can't cancel or nonrenew policies because the producer was terminated.
beats.say: The insurer can't cancel or nonrenew policies because the producer was terminated.

beats.text: Home and auto insurers may terminate an independent producer only for listed reasons, like malfeasance or fewer than 25 home and auto applications in 12 months, not mainly for location.
beats.say: Home and auto insurers may terminate an independent producer only for listed reasons, like malfeasance or fewer than twenty-five home and auto applications in twelve months, not mainly for location.

scenes.title: Michigan Property and Casualty Guaranty Association

items.label: Who belongs
items.detail: Insurers authorized for lines other than life or disability; surplus lines insurers are not members

items.label: Unearned premium
items.detail: Covered up to the first $500 per person; no refund under $50

items.label: $5 million claim cap
items.detail: Workers' comp and no-fault PIP claims are not capped

items.label: $25 million net worth
items.detail: No claims by or against an insured worth more than this

items.label: 30 days
items.detail: In-force policies continue no more than 30 days after the receiver is appointed

beats.text: When an insurer is insolvent, the Michigan Property and Casualty Guaranty Association pays covered claims. Insurers authorized for lines other than life or disability belong; surplus lines insurers don't.
beats.say: When an insurer is insolvent, the Michigan Property and Casualty Guaranty Association pays covered claims. Insurers authorized for lines other than life or disability belong; surplus lines insurers don't.

beats.text: Unearned premium: up to the first $500 per person, and no refund under $50.
beats.say: Unearned premium: up to the first five hundred dollars per person, and no refund under fifty dollars.

beats.text: Claims are capped at $5 million, except workers' comp and no-fault PIP. And no claims by or against an insured worth over $25 million.
beats.say: Claims are capped at five million dollars, except workers' comp and no-fault P I P. And no claims by or against an insured worth over twenty-five million dollars.

beats.text: Policies last no more than 30 days after the receiver is appointed. The dollar maximums are inflation-adjusted bases; exam items may use base or current figures.
beats.say: Policies last no more than thirty days after the receiver is appointed. The dollar maximums are inflation-adjusted bases; exam items may use base or current figures.

scenes.q: Michigan's guaranty association caps covered claims at $5 million (statutory base). Which claim against an insolvent insurer is NOT subject to that cap?
scenes.why: The per-claim cap does not apply to workers' compensation claims or no-fault PIP claims.

beats.text: Which claim against an insolvent insurer is NOT subject to the guaranty association's cap? Pick an answer.
beats.say: Which claim against an insolvent insurer is NOT subject to the guaranty association's cap? Pick an answer.

reveal.text: The no-fault PIP claim. PIP and workers' comp claims aren't capped.
reveal.say: The no-fault P I P claim. P I P and workers' comp claims aren't capped.

items: Fire policy: ACV, fire and lightning, 12:01 a.m., $25 minimum
Pay in 30 days after proof; sue within 1 year, tolled
Appraisal: 20 days to name, 15 to agree on an umpire, any 2 of 3
Home termination: 30 days, or 20 in the first 55; each reason
TRIA 20% and 80%; MPCGA cap spares PIP and workers' comp

beats.text: To recap. Fire policies: actual cash value, payment within 30 days of proof, a year to sue. Appraisal: 20 days, then 15.
beats.say: To recap. Fire policies: actual cash value, payment within thirty days of proof, a year to sue. Appraisal: twenty days, then fifteen.

beats.text: Home terminations: 30 days, or 20 in the first 55. TRIA: 20% deductible, 80% federal. The guaranty cap spares PIP and workers' comp.
beats.say: Home terminations: thirty days, or twenty in the first fifty-five. T R I A: twenty percent deductible, eighty percent federal. The guaranty cap spares P I P and workers' comp.
